Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
I went 10-years without a full-sized propane grill after moving.  We started camping not long after the move, so I used my portable camping grill (from another brand) both at home and while camping.  Two years ago we bought a vacation property and got a Spirit II E-210 to use there.  It was a great choice because of the extra space, two burners, and moving away from 1-lb propane cannisters.  Heat is consistent and adjustable.  I also appreciate the larger wheels for moving the grill and the ability to fold down the left side table. The spring actuated propane gauge has worked well enough to keep me from running out while grilling.

This year we decided to upgrade our home grilling abilities and I looked to Weber again.  I considered the Spirit EX-315 at a membership store, but ruled it out because of the electronic temperature gauge and small wheels.  After ruling out that bigger model, it made sense to get the same Spirit II E210 as we have at our other place. It will be easy to switch back and forth between operating the two grills.

I'm giving this grill only 3-stars, and here's why.  First, almost all of the best in-grill accessories from Weber are made for the 300-series grills and above.  Second, two burners are not ideal for indirect cooking.  Third, Weber took out the iGrill feature to save money but didn't spend the money to print a 200-series user manual that doesn't reference this feature.  Fourth, this new grill runs at least 100-degrees hotter than our original grill of the same model.   And finally, the influence Weber has over the sales channels can create a poor purchasing experience.  I had multiple options and went with a locally owned franchise hardware store who a) assembled the fuel gauge wrong, and b) were very reluctant to address a pricing promotion that started very shortly after my purchase.
Results.Title: Huge Step Up From A Portable Gas Grill

Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
I had purchased an Oklahoma Joe Tahoma 900, thinking it would get hot enough to be able to do both my grilling and smoking. And it can, but it is not really designed for that, and you go through a ton of charcoal to get it up to 500 degrees.

I had a weber spirit 3 burner before that I used lovingly for 10 years, but eventually it just was getting too hard to keep up and there was some rust, etc... 

Sooooo... I did a week's worth of research on getting a cheap gas grill for my weekday grilling (I grill something 3 or 4 nights a week) that is simple. Light it, wait until its hot and grill it.
I went to multiple stores (Lowes, Home Depot, Menards, Ace Hardware) and checked out the 'cheap' ones, and lets just say you get what you pay for. Some were okay, but I could tell they would be falling apart in a couple years. 

So, my recommendation is pay up for the quality. The weber E-210 is almost the perfect small deck/patio grill. Assembly was a little hard for my 60 year-old knees, but wasn't particularly hard (note: put something down underneath on a deck... I lost 2 screws that fell through the deck and had to go to the hardware store to replace). It lit and fired up the first time. I already have a Bluetooth remote meat probe, so no need to pay extra for the built in ones. 

Also, I liked that the propane tank hangs on the side with easy access. With my old Weber, it had a cabinet underneath (that was useless and just collected dirt and grime) and bending over with a heavy propane tank  and hanging it inside the cabinet was a pain. 

Two burners is more than enough for a family of 4 and you can be eating at the table in same time it takes to pre-heat a pellet grill or charcoal. Trust me... I've used them all.
Results.Title: Nothing rewards like quality

Open the door to the world of grilling with crazy good food and friends coming together. Equipped with the powerful GS4 grilling system, this two burner gas grill is your entry to the Weber family and to everyday grilling. The compact open-cart design and the practical folding side table makes it fit even on small spaces, and you have all the basics you need to get familiar with gas grilling. So whether it’s a busy Monday or a relaxed Sunday – invite a couple of friends over, push the ignition and enjoy the special atmosphere that surrounds the grill.
